review_comments_data.body: I just added the jiff lib to generate the diff but it seems the lib throws an error when applying the patch, I'm still investigating it. @IanMayo

I decided to use this lib https://www.npmjs.com/package/fast-json-patch, it seems better in terms of performance and it solves the error of jiff lib. The only small problem I have is that after the c/u/d feature and reloading the page, all the features are gone. I'm still working on it but I welcome you to check this out. @IanMayo
@lebaphi  - can we please keep knowledge of deltas, and how to create/merge them inside `core-mapping`?
To do the above, I _think_ we just call `handleNonInfoMessage` (as before), and then handle the new `messages` in `CoreMapping`

I think I've got it. Our current `delta` handling is in `handleNewMessage`.  That method doesn't get called when we load an existing wargame.
So, I think the `delta` handling has to happen in `CoreMapping`.  Then it will run on initial load aswell as on new messages.
I see, I will try this 👍

Aah, @lebaphi - there is another bit of logic we can use here.  If there **isn't** a `lastMessage` then we send the whole `newFeatureCollection` as a `MAPPING_MESSAGE`.

At some point in the future we will need to consider when we send these whole messages.  But, when do come up with something, we will just have to clear `lastMessage` - and know that the full `featureCollection` will be sent.

issues.title: Core Mapping - support for generating message deltas
issues.body:
To reduce the size of the MappingMessage objects, we should start working with deltas.

We'll support this by `MappingMessage` having either a `featureCollection` or a `featureDelta`.

When the shapes on the map are changed (C, U or D), we should calculate the delta of the feature collection, and send this as a new message for that channel.

So, the wargame database will contain an initial `featureCollection` and then a series of `featureDelta` messages.

Note: let's use this library to generate the diffs: https://github.com/cujojs/jiff

**Update:** -  unless you prefer a different implementation @lebaphi   We could use one that includes TypeScript definitions, if you prefer that.
